links.targetTitle: The weekly Atlas edit path demands twice the Yes vote-weight

title: Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposals need an absolute floor of Yes votes, not merely a majority
content:
A.1.11.2.4 sets a Minimum Positive Participation requirement: "Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle Proposals must have at least 480,000,000 SKY equivalents of Yes votes to be accepted."

The structural point is that this is an absolute affirmative threshold, not a quorum on total participation and not a relative margin. An amendment with overwhelming support among a handful of voters fails; an amendment with modest opposition but broad support passes. Apathy therefore reads as rejection rather than as consent.

This is the main counterweight to the weekly cycle's otherwise light machinery, where a three-day Poll produces a direct edit to the Atlas without any Executive Vote. Requiring a large mass of active Yes weight makes low-attention windows — holidays, crises, quiet weeks — unusable for pushing through changes, which is exactly when a cheap amendment path would be most dangerous.

The cost is a status-quo bias that is not neutral between kinds of change. Uncontroversial cleanup needs the same mobilization as a contested rewrite, so housekeeping-grade Atlas edits can fail purely for lack of interest — which is part of why the Atlas maintains separate lighter routes for genuinely low-stakes work.
description: At least 480,000,000 SKY equivalents must vote Yes for acceptance, so low-turnout amendments fail even when unopposed.
